current_example.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to $\log x ?$ 

I. $\dfrac {\log_{2} x} {\log_{2} 10}$

II. $\dfrac {\log_{2} 10} {\log_{2} x}$

III. $\log_{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{10}\right)$
current_example.worked_solution:
The change of base formula for logarithms is

$$
\log_a X = \dfrac {\log_b X} {\log_b a}.
$$

The change of base formula works with any new base. In this example, the choices are written using base $2,$ so we rewrite $\log x$ in terms of $\log_2.$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡x & ={log}_{10}⁡x \\  & =\frac{{log}_{2}⁡x}{{log}_{2}⁡10}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "I only."
